hints: In right $\triangle OAT$, tangent length $AT = r\tan\theta$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the circular arc length $AB$ with central angle $2\theta$:
$$\text{Arc } AB = r(2\theta) = 2r\theta$$

By symmetry, the line $OT$ bisects angle $\angle AOB$, so $\angle AOT = \theta$. In right-angled triangle $\triangle OAT$ ($AT \perp OA$):
$$AT = OA\tan\theta = r\tan\theta$$
$$BT = r\tan\theta$$

Sum the boundary components to express the perimeter of the shaded region:
$$\text{Perimeter} = \text{Arc } AB + AT + BT = 2r\theta + 2r\tan\theta = 2r(\theta + \tan\theta)$$

hints: Subtract to find shaded area $\approx 34.3\text{ cm}^2$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the area of quadrilateral $OATB$ (composed of two congruent right-angled triangles $\triangle OAT$ and $\triangle OBT$) with $r = 5, \theta = 1.2$:
$$\text{Area}(OATB) = 2 \times \left(\frac{1}{2} \times r \times r\tan\theta\right) = r^2\tan\theta = 5^2\tan(1.2) = 25\tan(1.2) \approx 25(2.57215) \approx 64.3038\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of sector $OAB$ (radius $5\text{ cm}$, central angle $2\theta = 2.4\text{ radians}$):
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector } OAB) = \frac{1}{2}r^2(2\theta) = \frac{1}{2}(25)(2.4) = 30\text{ cm}^2$$

Subtract the sector area from the quadrilateral area:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = 64.3038 - 30 = 34.3038 \approx 34.3\text{ cm}^2 \quad (\text{to 3 s.f.})$$
